text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovakia's natural gas consumption is expected to increase to 4.8 billion cubic metres by the year 2000, and to seven billion in 2010, from the current 3.3 billion cubic metres.
- The overall volume of gas transported through Slovakia from Russia is expected to increase to 92 billion cubic metres in the year 2000, from the current 79 billion.
- The finance ministry has not yet decided on the appeal of the investment company PSIS, manager of the largest investment fund Sporofond, against the withdrawal of its licence last June.

- The Slovak Association of Beer and Malt Producers has asked the Agriculture Ministry to limit beer imports to 200,000 hectolitres a year. Production capacity of Slovakia's breweries is some 6.3 million hectolitres a year, but actual production is only some 4.6 million hectolitres. Beer imports total some 600,000 hectolitres a year.
NARODNA OBRODA - Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene has cancelled his Thursday visit to Slovakia due to urgent domestic affairs.

- Slovak Defence Minister Jan Sitek on Thursday leaves on a three-day official visit to Russia. Sitek is scheduled to meet Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov to discuss European security issues and deliveries of Russian military equipment as a part of repayment of Russian debt to Slovakia.

PRAVDA - Sitek, from the Slovak National Party (SNS), a junior member of the ruling coalition, said his party would not support the 1997 state budget in parliament if the military budget is not increased to at least 14.3 billion crowns, from the proposed 13.6 billion.
